categories.main_business_segments: IAC operates through four primary reportable segments: Dotdash Meredith (digital and print publishing with over 40 brands including PEOPLE, Better Homes & Gardens, and Verywell), Angi Inc. (home services marketplace connecting professionals with consumers across 500+ categories), Search (Ask Media Group and Desktop providing search services and information), and Emerging & Other (Care.com for caregiving services, Mosaic Group for mobile applications, and other ventures). The company also holds meaningful stakes in external companies like MGM Resorts International and Vivian Health.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: IAC's core technologies include proprietary algorithms for matching consumers with service professionals and caregivers, digital content management and distribution platforms, search engine optimization and paid search capabilities, mobile application development and distribution through app stores, and data analytics for user targeting and personalization. Production methods vary by segment: Dotdash Meredith produces digital content and print magazines; Angi Inc. operates digital marketplaces and pre-priced service platforms; Search provides algorithmic and paid search results; and Mosaic Group develops subscription mobile applications.
categories.primary_customers_markets: IAC serves diverse customer bases: consumers seeking home services, caregiving solutions, publishing content, and search information; service professionals and caregivers seeking customer connections; advertisers and marketers seeking audience reach; employers seeking employee benefits; and families seeking care solutions. Primary end markets include home services and improvement, caregiving and family services, digital publishing and media, online search and information, and mobile applications across entertainment, lifestyle, health, and business categories.
categories.geographic_coverage: IAC operates primarily in the United States, with significant operations in the United Kingdom, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Italy, and Canada through Angi Inc.'s international segment. The company has corporate headquarters in New York and owns facilities in Des Moines, Iowa. Dotdash Meredith operates digital and print publishing brands serving North American audiences, while Mosaic Group operates globally across 192 countries with applications in 28 languages.
categories.supply_chain_position: IAC operates primarily in the downstream and midstream positions of various supply chains. Dotdash Meredith is a content publisher and advertiser-supported media company. Angi Inc. operates as a marketplace intermediary connecting service professionals with consumers. Search operates as an information intermediary. Care.com operates as a marketplace for caregiving services. Mosaic Group distributes applications through third-party app stores. The company relies on third-party suppliers for paper, printing, distribution, and technology infrastructure.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: IAC's strategic priorities include expanding digital reach and monetization of publishing brands, growing pre-priced service offerings at Angi Inc., optimizing search engine marketing efficiency, developing mobile applications and subscription services, expanding enterprise solutions at Care.com, and investing in emerging businesses like Vivian Health. R&D focuses on product development, technology infrastructure scalability, artificial intelligence applications, mobile platform optimization, and data analytics capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: IAC generates revenue through multiple models: advertising (digital display and programmatic ads), subscription fees (print magazines, mobile apps, care services), performance marketing and affiliate commissions, paid search listings (primarily from Google), consumer connection fees and service professional advertising (Angi Inc.), enterprise solutions contracts, and licensing agreements. Revenue is primarily transaction-based and subscription-based, with significant reliance on advertising expenditures and Google partnership revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: IAC competes with major search engines (Google, Microsoft, Yahoo), social media platforms (Facebook, Amazon), online marketplaces, traditional media companies, and specialized competitors in each segment. In publishing, competitors include diversified media companies and online publishers. In home services, competitors include search engines, local directories, and traditional word-of-mouth methods. In caregiving, competitors include traditional offline resources and other online platforms. IAC positions itself as a category leader in its core segments with strong brand portfolios and digital-first strategies.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2022, IAC had approximately 11,000 employees and generated revenue across multiple segments. The company had total debt of approximately $2.1 billion (Dotdash Meredith Term Loans and ANGI Group Senior Notes). IAC is a large accelerated filer on NASDAQ under ticker IAC. The company has experienced growth through acquisitions (Meredith in 2021, Care.com in 2020) and organic expansion, though certain segments like Print face declining revenue trends requiring strategic management.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: IAC's value proposition centers on category-leading brands with strong consumer trust and recognition, proprietary technology platforms for efficient matching and discovery, comprehensive content and information resources, quality screening and safety measures for service professionals and caregivers, and integrated solutions spanning multiple consumer needs. Differentiation includes large-scale digital reach, diverse brand portfolios, data-driven targeting capabilities, and established marketplace networks with network effects that create switching costs and competitive advantages.
